description: Horizon sweep: angle (deg) of Euler-integrated states to the analytic fixed point, and Euler-vs-RK45 angle, vs integration time T. Same tokens tracked across T (worst-8 chosen at T=30).
median_floor_note: median angles ~0.02 deg (float32) are the arccos resolution floor near cos=1 (~sqrt(2*eps_f32)); float64 recompute (median_deg_float64) shows the true residual. Not a physical quantity.

notes.finite_horizon_slow_escape: Some tokens (e.g. TinyStories token 2322: 120.7deg at T=30; KWS token 2740) initialize near the unstable/antipodal equilibrium and have not reached the analytic fixed point at the inference horizon T=30. The max angle to the analytic point decays monotonically with T (see horizon_sweep.json: TS 120.7->44.5deg, KWS 148.8->22.1deg out to T=3000) and BOTH integrators track it. Finite-horizon effect, not a discrepancy; the analytic fixed point remains the attractor.
notes.euler_stiffness_single_token: One token (TinyStories token 2429, ||h||=1575.1, generic init 85.9deg to analytic / 94.1deg to antipode) is a fixed-step-Euler failure, NOT finite-horizon and NOT a theory effect: RK45 converges to the analytic fixed point exactly (0.0000deg at T=30, 300, 3000) while forward Euler (dt=0.05) is unstable at this large ||h|| and stays 44.48deg away at every T. Adaptive RK45 and the analytic fixed point agree; only fixed-step Euler fails. This is why the paper computes the fixed point analytically rather than by fixed-step integration.
notes.median_note: Median angles ~0.02deg (float32) are the arccos resolution floor near cos=1; float64 recompute gives the true residual (see median_deg_float64 in horizon_sweep.json).
